hypothesis: The previous development attempt failed on n=256 because its row-tile kernel covered the full x extent instead of the active interior. This candidate restricts each static z/y row to x0..x1 and tests direct collapsed row-level scheduling against the prior tiling approach. The serial cutoff remains for small workloads; one-thread calls use a region per timestep and larger budgets use one persistent team. Existing aggregate results show five distinct valid candidates, with the best at 0.2292 s versus the 0.4575 s baseline, but do not establish per-budget effects; no speedup is claimed here.
notes: No commands were executed. The controller must verify complete outputs and boundaries on the small cases and n=256, then measure the official one- and four-core settings; this proposal makes no new correctness or performance claim.
transformations: Replaced tiled row worksharing with static collapsed z/y row worksharing, with each row computing only x0..x1.
Retained the serial baseline path and its low-work cutoff.
Used a separate OpenMP parallel-for region per timestep for a one-thread budget, and one persistent team with the implicit per-step worksharing barrier for larger budgets.
Preserved the six-step ping-pong order, initialization, stencil arithmetic and boundary write bounds; made no SIMD or temporal-blocking changes.
